findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the terminal inline fold is placed in the shared archive engine seam (the archive `*_core`/`_seam.append_event` write path) so library-facade and MCP archive ingress inherit it, not only the leaf.py CLI command — or state explicitly that leaf.archive is the single shared archive write path for all three ingress surfaces.
evidence: 'leaf.archive (src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py) writes only the ARCHIVED event + .archived marker'
'make the fold part of the archive operation itself: rebar archive performs the ticket's final fold inline'
'with change 1 in place, an archived ticket really IS folded on its way out' — the default-scoping invariant depends on every archive path folding
Bypassing ingress paths: library facade rebar.archive and the MCP archive tool handler, if they do not route through leaf.archive
findings.finding: Change 1 places the terminal inline fold inside `leaf.archive` in src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py (the CLI command module). If `archive` is also reachable via a library facade (rebar.archive) or an MCP archive tool that does not delegate to this same leaf function, those ingress paths would write the ARCHIVED event + `.archived` marker WITHOUT the inline fold. Because change 2's default active-only scoping relies on the invariant that an archived ticket is already fully folded (default sweeps never revisit it), any bypassing archive path would silently strand unfolded tail events on the archived ticket. The plan does not state that leaf.archive is the single shared archive write path across all three ingress surfaces.
findings.location: Scope: 'src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py — archive performs the ticket's terminal fold inline before the ARCHIVED event.'
scenarios: A caller invoking the library archive facade (or MCP archive tool) archives a ticket with unfolded tail events; the inline fold never runs; default compact-all then skips the archived dir; the tail events are permanently stranded (no SNAPSHOT covers them).
The archive-time-fold invariant holds only for the CLI, so the 'nothing stranded' acceptance criterion is true for CLI archive but false for other ingress paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the terminal fold into the shared archive core/write function that CLI, library facade, and MCP archive tool all delegate to, so the 'archived => folded' invariant is inherited by every ingress path before change 2 flips the default.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the fsck_scan.py scope description to distinguish the two REPORTING-only loops (JSON-validity, create-events — always walk all tickets for the store-wide authorship tally, gate only reporting on archival state) from the two loops (snapshot-consistency, forward-compat) that may actually scope their walk active-only.
evidence: fsck_scan.py:61 and :98 — _check_json_validity and _check_create_events call `_ticket_dirs(tracker, include_archived=True)` UNCONDITIONALLY; their `reported = include_archived or not _dir_is_archived(...)` gate scopes only which findings are emitted, not the walk.

fsck_scan.py docstrings 52-57 and 83-88: 'That tally is a STORE-WIDE metric, so this check always walks every ticket dir; include_archived scopes only which dirs' findings are REPORTED.' The per-env tally feeds check 4.9 (_tracker_health) and _advisory_lines (signed/unsigned totals).
By contrast only _check_ticket_snapshots (186) and _check_forward_compat (229) actually pass `include_archived=include_archived` into the walk.
findings.finding: The plan describes ALL fsck scan loops as switching to the active-only iterator, but two of the per-ticket loops (JSON-validity and create-events checks) feed STORE-WIDE authorship tallies and must keep walking every ticket; only their REPORTING may be scoped by archival state.
findings.location: Approach step 2 ('Switch the fsck scan loops to it') and Scope bullet 'src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py — scan loops take the shared active-only iterator; include_archived threading.'
scenarios: An implementer follows the plan's literal 'scan loops take the shared active-only iterator' and scopes the JSON-validity / create-events loops active-only, silently truncating the store-wide signed/unsigned authorship tally and the per-env authorship health check to active tickets.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 2 and the fsck_scan.py Scope bullet, replace 'the fsck scan loops' / 'scan loops take the shared active-only iterator' with: the snapshot-consistency and forward-compat loops take the active-only iterator, while the JSON-validity and create-events loops (which sum store-wide authorship tallies) keep walking all tickets and gate only whether each dir's findings are REPORTED on include_archived.

fsck_scan.py `_check_json_validity` and `_check_create_events` call `_ticket_dirs(tracker, include_archived=True)` unconditionally and scope only `reported`, because they sum a store-wide authorship tally
findings.finding: The plan's Approach step 2 ('Switch the fsck scan loops to it') and its performance rationale imply the entire fsck scan becomes active-only, but two fsck checks (JSON-validity / env-authorship tally and CREATE-events / store-wide signed-unsigned tally) compute STORE-WIDE metrics that must keep walking every archived ticket dir; only their REPORTING can be scoped. The plan under-specifies which loops become active-only vs. which stay full-walk-but-report-scoped, and overstates the fsck performance win.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword AC1 (and Approach step 1) to state the SNAPSHOT covers all events PRECEDING the ARCHIVED event, and that the single trailing ARCHIVED event is expected-and-harmless (never folded, default walk skips the dir).
evidence: Plan: 'performs the ticket's final fold inline right before writing the ARCHIVED event'
Plan AC1: 'SNAPSHOT covers all its events'
leaf.py archive(): `_terminal_fold(...)` then `append_event(resolved, "ARCHIVED", ...)` — the ARCHIVED event postdates the fold
findings.finding: The archive terminal fold runs BEFORE the ARCHIVED event is appended, so the ARCHIVED event is written after the fold and is never captured by the SNAPSHOT. The AC 'SNAPSHOT covers all its events' is therefore literally unsatisfiable — a just-archived ticket always carries exactly one trailing unfolded event (the ARCHIVED event itself).
findings.location: Approach step 1; AC line 1 ('`rebar archive` folds the ticket inline (SNAPSHOT covers all its events) before writing ARCHIVED')
scenarios: Sequence test asserts the SNAPSHOT source_event_uuids covers the ARCHIVED event and fails, or the AC is read as requiring a second fold that would defeat the point
